page: Amazon Web Services inf2.xlarge is an accelerated computing instance hosted on the AWS Nitro hypervisor platform. It combines general-purpose x86_64 processing with specialized machine learning hardware, featuring an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor operating at 3.6 GHz with 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores and 16 GB of DDR4 memory. The primary accelerator is a single AWS Inferentia2 chip equipped with 32 GB of dedicated accelerator memory. Local instance storage is not included, and baseline network throughput is rated at 2 Gbps with no complimentary public IPv4 addresses included.

Benchmark metrics demonstrate a clear performance dichotomy between single-thread CPU tasks and broader system operations. Single-core processing shows strong capability, reaching 2965.49 in stress-ng tests and an average score of 1659.0 in Geekbench. In contrast, multi-threaded CPU output ranks in the lower tiers due to the two-core physical limit, scoring 5927.07 on stress-ng multi-core and 3748.0 on Geekbench multi-core. System memory bandwidth remains limited, registering 38.44 GB/sec for uncached read operations, which contributes to lower percentiles in Redis SET throughput and standard database benchmarks.

The inf2.xlarge provides qualitative cost efficiency for targeted deep learning inference deployments rather than general-purpose CPU tasks. Standard CPU-based LLM benchmarks drop sharply from 153.84 tokens per second on a 135M model to 6.57 tokens per second on a 7B model, reinforcing that workloads must leverage the Inferentia2 silicon and its 32 GB accelerator memory to realize efficiency gains. The instance serves primarily as an inference engine for natural language processing, computer vision, and machine learning models tailored to the AWS Neuron software ecosystem.
description: Amazon Web Services inf2.xlarge is an accelerated computing instance designed for machine learning inference workloads. Running on the Nitro hypervisor, the host configuration includes an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor operating at 3.6 GHz with 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores, 16 GB of DDR4 system RAM, and 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, with no integrated local storage. Hardware acceleration is provided by one AWS Inferentia2 processor equipped with 32 GB of dedicated memory. Benchmark data indicates solid single-core CPU throughput, while multi-threaded compute, system memory bandwidth, and standard Redis or database operations rank in lower percentiles due to the limited two-core CPU allocation. The instance provides a resource-efficient target specifically for deploying compatible deep learning and neural network inference models suited to the Inferentia2 architecture, rather than conventional general-purpose compute, database management, or high-throughput network applications.
